explanation: Compared with the BVAS definition of Demri–Jurdziński–Lachish–Lazić (FSTTCS 2009), the open-problem statement in Bizière–Hilaire–Leroux–Sutre (MFCS 2025) and the 2026 preprint arXiv:2607.09558 (Bizière–Leroux–Sutre), whose abstract claims to 'solve the reachability problem for branching vector addition systems'. Reachable is the standard inductive definition (axioms; v + r for unary rules; v1 + v2 + r for binary rules; every intermediate configuration must be in ℕ^d), with axioms outside ℕ^d harmlessly ignored. The instance encodes (d, b, t) as d with lists of integer entries via a primitive recursive left inverse, so ComputablePred is the usual uniform decidability with d part of the input. Faithful.
